newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: First Ireland proposes capital reorganisation.
newsitem.headline: First Ireland proposes capital reorganisation.

text.p: First Ireland Investment Company on Thursday announced proposals designed to reduce the discount of its share price to its net asset value.
The company said it was proposing a capital reorganisation which would involve replacing each shareholder's existing ordinary shares with new ordinary shares and loan stock units.
The move is in response to First Ireland's concern that the market value of its ordinary shares does not provide a fair reflection of the value of its underlying assets.
As of June 30, 1997, First Ireland's net asset value (NAV) was 171 pence per ordinary share while its share price was 153.5 pence, a discount of around 10 percent.
The company said it believed the discount was due primarily to an excess of supply over demand for the ordinary shares in the market.

"First Ireland will be able to redeem or purchase loan stock units. The board believes that doing so will have the effect of redressing the supply and demand imbalance and of narrowing the discount to fully diluted NAV at which First Ireland's new securities trade," it said.
